reflection.text:
Unblinded compound was emetine (CID 10219) with truth protein synthesis, while I called microtubule stabilizers at 0.55. I was driven by extreme and reproducible nuclear irregularity across four wells (nuc_form_factor z -33.7 to -47.9, nuc_solidity z -33.1 to -57.2) plus raised actin texture in e2, e3, e6, e7, and by compare_to_reference_atlas e5 voting 2/2 stabilizers with 7/10 k-neighbours as stabilizers.

What misled me was treating toxic nuclear fragmentation as stabilizer-like multinucleation. The atlas comparison e8 was actually split 2/4 stabilizers with per-well 1-NN 2x stabilizers (1 and 10 uM) vs 2x Eg5 inhibitors (0.3 and 3 uM), and dose_response showed no dose trend for frac_multinucleate_proxy rho -0.20 p=0.8, frac_mitotic_like rho +0.60 p=0.4, and cell_count rho +0.00 p=1.0. My acquisition choice sampled only saturated mid-high doses 0.3, 1, 3, 10 uM with 2-field describe_phenotype e4 suggesting Aurora/Eg5, and I never sampled 0.01-0.1 uM onset or tested translation, so a protein-synthesis shutdown with secondary cell stress and death looked like a mitotic defect.

In retrospect the flat dose-responses and split NSC vote were warnings of a non-specific saturated phenotype rather than support for stabilizers, and the microscopist note of lower density vs DMSO was more consistent with cytotoxic translation inhibition (PMID 4347870, PMID 191850) than with a clean stabilizer arrest.
what_was_right: Noted reduced density/cell loss vs DMSO in e4, consistent with cytotoxic protein-synthesis shutdown rather than pure cytostatic mitotic arrest.
Measured flat/non-significant dose trends: frac_multinucleate_proxy rho -0.20 p=0.8 and cell_count rho 0.0 p=1.0, which correctly indicated a saturated non-dose-dependent phenotype.
Recorded split atlas evidence e8 and protocol per-well 2 vs 2 split (stabilizers vs Eg5 inhibitors), which correctly signaled low confidence rather than a definitive stabilizer match.
what_was_wrong: Misread extreme nuc_form_factor and nuc_solidity drops plus act_glcm_contrast +21 to +27 in e2, e3, e6, e7 as stabilizer-specific multinucleation/tubulin increase.

Over-relied on compare_to_reference_atlas e5/e8 k-neighbours favouring microtubule stabilizers 7/10 then 5/10, ignoring that fragmented/stressed nuclei from translation inhibition can mimic irregular mitotic nuclei and that the atlas forced a cytoskeletal call.

Acquisition choice sampled only 0.3-10 uM without low-dose 0.01-0.1 uM onset and used only 2 fields for e4, anchoring hypotheses to Aurora/Eg5/stabilizers and never acquiring a translation or tubulin-direct test.

citations.claim: Emetine inhibits protein synthesis as its proposed amebicide mechanism (PMID 4347870).
Emetine was studied alongside pactamycin as a protein synthesis inhibitor in behavioral pharmacology (PMID 191850).

reflection.next_experiment: Direct translation assay in the same cell line (puromycin incorporation/SUnSET or 35S-methionine) across 0.01-10 uM emetine with cycloheximide as protein-synthesis control and paclitaxel as stabilizer control, paired with anti-tubulin immunofluorescence and cell-free tubulin polymerization to test whether microtubules are directly stabilized.

## Conclusion

Verdict: approve.

Clean. ## Unblinding

Compound: **emetine** (PubChem CID [10219](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/10219))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Protein synthesis**.

## Reflection

Unblinded compound was emetine (CID 10219) with truth protein synthesis, while I called microtubule stabilizers at 0.55. I was driven by extreme and reproducible nuclear irregularity across four wells (nuc_form_factor z -33.7 to -47.9, nuc_solidity z -33.1 to -57.2) plus raised actin texture in e2, e3, e6, e7, and by compare_to_reference_atlas e5 voting 2/2 stabilizers with 7/10 k-neighbours as stabilizers.

What misled me was treating toxic nuclear fragmentation as stabilizer-like multinucleation. The atlas comparison e8 was actually split 2/4 stabilizers with per-well 1-NN 2x stabilizers (1 and 10 uM) vs 2x Eg5 inhibitors (0.3 and 3 uM), and dose_response showed no dose trend for frac_multinucleate_proxy rho -0.20 p=0.8, frac_mitotic_like rho +0.60 p=0.4, and cell_count rho +0.00 p=1.0. My acquisition choice sampled only saturated mid-high doses 0.3, 1, 3, 10 uM with 2-field describe_phenotype e4 suggesting Aurora/Eg5, and I never sampled 0.01-0.1 uM onset or tested translation, so a protein-synthesis shutdown with secondary cell stress and death looked like a mitotic defect.

In retrospect the flat dose-responses and split NSC vote were warnings of a non-specific saturated phenotype rather than support for stabilizers, and the microscopist note of lower density vs DMSO was more consistent with cytotoxic translation inhibition (PMID 4347870, PMID 191850) than with a clean stabilizer arrest.

What was right:
- Noted reduced density/cell loss vs DMSO in e4, consistent with cytotoxic protein-synthesis shutdown rather than pure cytostatic mitotic arrest.
- Measured flat/non-significant dose trends: frac_multinucleate_proxy rho -0.20 p=0.8 and cell_count rho 0.0 p=1.0, which correctly indicated a saturated non-dose-dependent phenotype.
- Recorded split atlas evidence e8 and protocol per-well 2 vs 2 split (stabilizers vs Eg5 inhibitors), which correctly signaled low confidence rather than a definitive stabilizer match.

What was wrong or missed:
- Misread extreme nuc_form_factor and nuc_solidity drops plus act_glcm_contrast +21 to +27 in e2, e3, e6, e7 as stabilizer-specific multinucleation/tubulin increase.
- Over-relied on compare_to_reference_atlas e5/e8 k-neighbours favouring microtubule stabilizers 7/10 then 5/10, ignoring that fragmented/stressed nuclei from translation inhibition can mimic irregular mitotic nuclei and that the atlas forced a cytoskeletal call.
- Acquisition choice sampled only 0.3-10 uM without low-dose 0.01-0.1 uM onset and used only 2 fields for e4, anchoring hypotheses to Aurora/Eg5/stabilizers and never acquiring a translation or tubulin-direct test.

Proposed next experiment: Direct translation assay in the same cell line (puromycin incorporation/SUnSET or 35S-methionine) across 0.01-10 uM emetine with cycloheximide as protein-synthesis control and paclitaxel as stabilizer control, paired with anti-tubulin immunofluorescence and cell-free tubulin polymerization to test whether microtubules are directly stabilized.

## Citations

Citations verified: 2/2

- PMID [4347870](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/4347870/): Inhibition of protein synthesis: a mechanism of amebicide action of emetine and other structurally related compounds. *J Protozool* (1973) — Emetine inhibits protein synthesis as its proposed amebicide mechanism (PMID 4347870).
- PMID [191850](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/191850/): Protein synthesis and amnesia: studies with emetine and pactamycin. *Pharmacol Biochem Behav* (1977) — Emetine was studied alongside pactamycin as a protein synthesis inhibitor in behavioral pharmacology (PMID 191850).
